answer.rationale: Finance mandates an 18% cost cut and the incumbent has explicitly refused to reopen price this cycle, so renew_incumbent and negotiate_terms are unlikely to satisfy the primary objective. memory_c2 records that switching primary supply to a low-cost vendor cut unit cost sharply with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing, which is the only inherited evidence directly supporting a cost-cutting switch under time pressure (14-day contract expiry). However, the line is at 94% of committed volume with no buffer, so any switch carries real delivery risk if onboarding claims don't hold this time or under current conditions. I want to verify memory_c2's archived record before committing capital-intensive action, and even if confirmed, I'd scope this as a small guarded test/parallel qualification of the new vendor rather than a full cutover, to avoid stacking cost-driven vendor risk on top of an already zero-buffer production schedule. Add_second_source and defer_decision don't resolve the expiring primary contract in time, and renewing without price relief fails the finance mandate outright.
